name: Vladimir Keil

education.notes: Studied at the University of Duisburg-Essen. Exact dates not publicly confirmed.

keyDecisions: Took an intern role inside Daimler's corporate innovation lab (Lab 1886) — product management, strategy, market research exposure inside a top-tier German industrial.
lessons: Corporate innovation labs (Lab 1886, Audi Denkwerkstatt etc) are an underrated German entry point — they give early-career operators exposure to enterprise procurement pain.
Procurement pain inside Daimler later became Lio's founding insight.

keyDecisions: Co-founded an EdTech business with his roommate in Munich — reached profitability by age 22.
lessons: A profitable side venture during university is the cheapest possible founder-school — it filters whether you can ship under constraints.
Roommate co-founder is high-trust, fast-iterate — a credible structure when neither founder has a track record yet.
careerSteps.notes: Achieved profitability at age 22 per public coverage. Exact company name not in surfaced sources.

careerSteps.company: Gabriel (AI startup, partnered with German federal police)
keyDecisions: Co-founded Gabriel in 2021 — an AI startup that partnered with the German federal police (BKA / 'German FBI').
Built government / law-enforcement credibility early — the same trust profile that later helped Lio close enterprise procurement deals.
lessons: German public-sector partnerships are a credible early venture-builder credential.
Stacking multiple founder reps before your breakthrough company is becoming standard — Keil had at least two before askLio.
careerSteps.notes: Per Y Combinator company profile / public talks.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Lio (originally askLio) in 2023 in Munich with Lukas Heinzmann and Till Wagner — friends from prior contexts.
Got into YC Summer 2023 batch — German-team founder route into the US accelerator network.
Picked agentic AI for enterprise procurement — the exact pain Keil hit at both Daimler (employee) and at his earlier startup (founder).
Raised a $30M Series A in March 2026 led by Andreessen Horowitz, with SV Angel, Harry Stebbings and YC participating — $33M cumulative.
Built dual offices in New York and Munich — kept German operating base while planting US revenue flag.
lessons: Personal-pain market signal: Keil hit procurement bottlenecks at both Daimler and his EdTech — building the tool that already failed him twice is the cleanest founding wedge.
YC Summer 2023 → a16z Series A within 2.5 years is the canonical AI-revolution velocity arc.
Dual-HQ (Munich operating + NY revenue) is the German fintech / enterprise SaaS template now — keep European cost base, plant US flag.
Multi-time founder before 25 is becoming the new normal — at least two prior ventures before the breakthrough is a recurring pattern.
careerSteps.notes: Lio (askLio) was YC S23. $30M Series A March 2026 led by a16z, total funding ~$33M. Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2026 AI. CEO of agentic-AI procurement platform spanning sourcing, negotiations, approvals.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & CEO of Lio (Munich + NY). $30M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (March 2026). Agentic AI for enterprise procurement; YC S23 alum.

Personal-pain market signal: build the procurement tool that already failed you twice (at Daimler and your EdTech).
